title: Take a part from a person's hand that keeps drifting while they hold it out
instruction: The person is holding out the yellow block for you on their palm. Take it from their hand and put it in the grey tray. Their hand keeps drifting while they wait, so follow it, lift the block straight up off the palm, and don't bump their hand.
context: When a coworker passes a part, tool or instrument, their outstretched hand never holds perfectly still: it drifts and wobbles in small, irregular loops while they wait. A helper has to follow it, take the part cleanly without knocking it off or bumping the hand, and put it away. Done by: assembly-line workers, mechanics' assistants and scrub nurses.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. Positions are given as (cm in front of the line through the bases, cm toward the left arm from the midpoint between the bases, cm above the table). A mock hand is held out over the table from the far side: a flat skin-coloured plastic palm plate (13 cm long toward the arms, 9 cm wide, 1.5 cm thick), level, its top face's middle starting at (30, -17, 8); on it, two skin-coloured plastic stops (1 x 5 cm, 1 cm tall), one at each end of the palm, centred 5.7 cm in front of and behind its middle; behind the palm (away from the arms), 1 mm from its far edge, a grey-blue forearm block (22 cm long, 6 cm wide, 3 cm tall, its top 0.5 cm below the palm's top). The forearm is carried at its far end by a stiff three-axis drive, so palm, stops and forearm move as one. A yellow plastic tool block (10 cm long toward the arms, 2.5 cm wide, 5.5 cm tall, 140 g) lies flat on the palm between the stops, 2 mm from each. A grey plastic open tray (16 x 14 cm inside, 1 cm floor and walls, walls 5 cm tall) stands on the table, square to the arm bases, its centre at (20, -40). The hand drifts from the start of the trial and never stops: with u the hand's clock in seconds, its offset from the start point is x = 1.8 sin(360 u / 3.8) + 1.5 sin(360 u / 14.6), y = 2.5 (1 - cos(360 u / 3.8)) + 2.0 sin(360 u / 16.6) + 0.8 sin(360 u / 6.7), z = 0.3 sin(360 u / 6.8) + 0.2 sin(360 u / 3.4) (cm, angles in degrees). It starts at rest; its clock runs at a pace that grows as a smoothstep from 0 to full over the first 2 s (u = t - 1 s from then on). Speeds are 2.1 to 5.6 cm/s; the palm moves within about 7 x 10 cm and 0.9 cm up and down, and never retraces its path.
scoring: Checked every 0.05 s against where the palm is at that moment. The block is in its seat while its centre is within 1.5 cm sideways of where it sits seated on the palm and within 1.5 cm above or below that height; the first time it is out, it was taken up if its centre was more than 1.5 cm above its seat and still within 1.5 cm sideways, and knocked off otherwise. It counts as taken once it has been taken up and its centre has been 3 cm or more above its seat. The robot bumps the hand if any part of it comes within 1 cm of the palm, the stops or the forearm. 1.0 if the block was taken up, the robot never bumped the hand, and the block ends resting in the tray (centre inside the walls, underside within 1 cm of the floor, still for 1 s). Otherwise, at the end: 0 if the block was knocked off or never left its seat; 0.5 if it rests in the tray (the robot bumped the hand); 0.25 if it was taken but doesn't end in the tray (dropped, or still held); 0 otherwise.
reset_notes: Stop the hand at its start point, lay the block on the palm between the stops, empty the tray, and start the hand's drift with the trial.
fidelity: The hand follows its path exactly, like a stiff drive: the arms can't push it or stop it, and it doesn't flinch or yield as a person's hand would; bumping it is judged by distance (1 cm), with the robot modelled as capsules larger than its parts (links 4 cm radius, gripper housing 5 cm, wrist camera 2.5 cm, fingers 8 mm). The hand is four boxes 1 mm apart moving as one. The block has rubber-like friction (1.2/1.0).
